candidates.old:
STA sky_stop
    LDA sky_ry,X
    CMP sky_stop
    BCC no                          \ after it
candidates.new:
STA sky_stop
    CMP sky_ry,X                    \ stop <= ry: after it if not
    BCC skyrow_in
    BNE no                          \ after it
.skyrow_in
candidates.summary: Compare the stored stop against sky_ry,X directly instead of reloading ry and comparing with sky_stop; passes on C=0 (stop<ry, branch taken to next-but-one) or Z=1 (equal), else no. Saves the LDA (4) and uses abs,X CMP (4) in place of zp CMP (3): 9 -> 7 cycles when stop<ry, 8 when stop==ry. Alternative to the BEQ-first candidate (overlapping).
candidates.equivalence: Old: reload A=ry, CMP stop, go to no iff ry < stop (C clear). New: A is still stop (just stored), CMP ry computes stop - ry: stop < ry (C=0) or stop == ry (Z=1) passes, stop > ry (C=1, Z=0) goes to no - the same unsigned condition ry >= stop, no wrap. sky_stop is stored before as before; A differs afterwards (old: ry, new: stop) but the next instruction, LDA sky_rl,X, overwrites A and the flags are dead (ORA follows later); X, Y untouched; on the no path A and flags are not read by callers (they test C, which 'no' sets with SEC). Flag-order: BCC first favours stop<ry, the common case for non-edge columns.
candidates.relies_on: Same size (9 bytes) as the old four lines, so nothing after them slides: no page-crossing moves. sky_col_row's tables (sky_rl..sky_ry, &BC90-&BCBA) are all in page &BC, so no indexed-read page cost changes. The taken/not-taken branch to the next-but-one instruction cannot cross a page (code at &DF2x). Callers (sky_col_check, sky_col_zero) read only X, C, s_ptr, Y and sky_stop on exit, never A or other flags; on 'no' exits sky_stop is not read. New label is local to sky_col_row's block and unique to this candidate.

    BCC no                          \ after it
candidates.new:
STA sky_stop
    CMP sky_ry,X                    \ stop <= ry: after it if not
    BEQ skyrow_eq
    BCS no                          \ after it
.skyrow_eq
candidates.summary: As the other candidate but BEQ first: 9 -> 8 cycles when stop<ry (BEQ and BCS both not taken), 7 when stop==ry (BEQ taken). Better only if the equal case (the rectangle's last column, as lead_col's right edge checks) dominates. Overlaps the BCC-first candidate; pick one.
